decision: Gate the operational calibrated-topology selection command in full, hosted distributed-fault, and local QA.

reviews.correctness: The operational command is the authority that composes duration-bound calibration with measured topology selection; component-only tests can pass while the production handoff regresses.
reviews.robustness: Hosted/local parity plus the existing parity test fails closed against future coverage drift.
reviews.latency_resources: One small deterministic Node test adds negligible CI/local cost and no qrexec, VM, worker, or production runtime overhead.
reviews.regression_risk: QA-only wiring is lower risk than modifying MissionQueue, coordinator, calibration transport, or Qubes services while hosted runner execution remains unstable.

alternatives_rejected: Rely on component calibration and evaluator tests only: misses composition/provenance handoff regressions.
Run only in full npm test: hosted distributed-fault and local fallback could drift.
Add live Qubes execution to every CI run: higher resource/latency cost and unavailable before Qubes qualification.
lessons: Operational authorities require direct QA coverage, not only their component modules.
Coverage parity is part of reliability when hosted CI and local fallback are both used.
safety: Synthetic/defensive calibration only; no financial transactions and no security controls weakened.
